title: Acute monoarthritis: gout or sepsis?
stem: Cubicle 30. Mr Siu, 58, woke with an extremely painful, red, swollen right big toe. He had a similar episode a year ago in the same toe. Temperature 37.6 °C. Take a history, examine the joint, and explain management.
notes:
Checked against EULAR 2016 gout recommendations, the BSR 2017 gout guideline, and NICE NG219 (Gout, 2022).

Acute gout: rapid onset (maximal within 24 hours), first MTP joint (podagra), triggers (alcohol, especially beer and spirits; purine-rich food; dehydration; diuretics; acute illness), recurrent episodes, tophi. Septic arthritis must be excluded when there is fever, systemic illness, or an atypical or prosthetic joint — aspirate. Diagnosis: joint aspiration with negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals (gold standard); serum urate may be normal during an attack.

Treat the flare: NSAID (with PPI) or colchicine 500 microgram two to four times daily (low-dose regimen) or oral prednisolone 30–35 mg for 3–5 days; ice, rest. Do not stop allopurinol during a flare if already taking it; urate-lowering therapy is offered after the flare (NICE NG219 offers it to people with recurrent flares; treat-to-target urate under 360 µmol/L, or 300 with tophi), with colchicine prophylaxis. Review cardiovascular risk and diuretics.

Your notes list polyarthritis and joint pain topics; nothing conflicts.

steps.hint: Likely gout; treat the flare; triggers; long-term urate lowering; when to return.

opts.t: This looks like gout — uric acid crystals in the joint. If you had a high fever or felt very unwell, we'd take fluid from the joint to exclude infection.
opts.mark: Explains gout and when to exclude sepsis

opts.t: Naproxen with omeprazole (or colchicine 500 microgram 2–4 times a day, or prednisolone if NSAIDs unsuitable); rest and ice
Reduce beer and seafood; ask your GP about changing the water tablet and starting urate-lowering treatment after the attack
opts.mark: Addresses triggers, diuretics and long-term urate lowering

opts.t: Start allopurinol today at a high dose to stop this attack
opts.r: Allopurinol doesn't treat the flare; start after it settles, with prophylaxis.
